method: Each in-figure reference value located in the repo, then checked against an authoritative public source (NIST Chemistry WebBook / NIST CODATA / CCCBDB, Martell & Smith via Harvey LibreTexts, Shannon 1976 via KnowledgeDoor, Wikipedia data pages that cite NIST/CRC). Verdicts: MATCH (value agrees at the figure precision), WITHIN_ROUNDING (agrees after rounding/truncation, difference noted), MISMATCH (disagrees), UNVERIFIED (could not establish).
limits: The CRC Handbook, the original Shannon paper text and NIST SRD 46 (Windows software) could not be read; values attributed to them rest on the secondary sources named per entry.

entries.figure: Claim A: Born-Haber cycle NaCl (kJ/mol, 298 K)
entries.quantity: Electron affinity of Cl, as DH of Cl(g)+e- -> Cl-(g)
entries.authoritativeValue: EA(Cl) = 3.612725 +/- 0.000087 eV (Trainham 1987), 3.613577 eV (Berzinsh 1995), 3.6131 eV (Martin & Hepburn 1998) = 348.6 kJ/mol (my conversion)

Strict 298 K enthalpy carries an RT-type correction (LibreTexts Mink NaCl page applies '-2RT' to the whole cycle: https://chem.libretexts.org/Courses/CSU_San_Bernardino/CHEM_4300%3A_Inorganic_Chemistry_(Mink)/10%3A_Ionic_and_Covalent_Solids_-_Energetics/10.04%3A_Born-Haber_Cycles_for_NaCl_and_Silver_Halides). Size of any 298 K correction was not looked up in a source.

entries.figure: Claim A: Born-Haber cycle NaCl (kJ/mol, 298 K)
entries.quantity: Lattice energy NaCl, as DH of Na+(g)+Cl-(g)->NaCl(s)
entries.authoritativeValue: Born-Haber-derived: -786 kJ/mol (Wikipedia 'Lattice energy', citing Shriver & Atkins). Closing the cycle with NIST inputs above gives -411.12 - (107.5 + 495.85 + 121.3 - 348.6) = -787.1. Range in textbooks/handbooks: ~ -776 (older data) / -786 to -788 (Born-Haber) vs ~ -766 to -770 (calculated ionic-model, e.g. OpenStax 769, LibreTexts Born-Mayer -766.5).
entries.source: Wikipedia Lattice energy: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lattice_energy ; OpenStax Chem 2e 7.5: https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/7-5-strengths-of-ionic-and-covalent-bonds ; LibreTexts Mink NaCl page (URL in EA row). CRC/Jenkins value 786 (thermochemical cycle) vs 769 (calculated) reported by a search snippet citing WebElements; the WebElements/Sheffield pages could not be fetched (account suspended) so that CRC figure is NOT directly confirmed.
entries.note: Yes: -787 is an experimental-data (Born-Haber-derived) value, not directly measured, and is NOT the ionic-model/Born-Lande value (about -766 to -770). SIGN CONVENTION: figure uses formation convention (negative, exothermic). OpenStax and the CRC style use the dissociation convention (+769/+786 etc.); Wikipedia states both are widely used. 1 kJ/mol off Wikipedia's 786 comes from input-set rounding.

entries.figure: Claim C: first ionisation energies, period 3 (kJ/mol)
entries.quantity: 'Dips at Al and S' pattern and explanation
entries.authoritativeValue: Mg 737.7 > Al 577.5 and P 1011.8 > S 999.6 (data above). Explanation: outer p electron is higher in energy and shielded by the filled s subshell (Mg->Al); in S the 4th p electron is the first to pair in a p orbital, and paired-electron repulsion/shielding makes it easier to remove (P->S).
entries.source: Wikipedia 'Ionization energy': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ionization_energy
entries.note: The page states the s-shielding argument explicitly for the period-2 analogue (Be->B) and the pairing/shielding argument for O, S, Se; applying both to period 3 is the standard textbook extension (the page does not spell out S separately).

entries.figure: chem.coord.stability (conceptSceneParams.ts:779-786), Claim H
entries.quantity: [Cu(NH3)4]2+ log Kf (bar labelled 'log Kf', value 13.0; the claim writes log beta4)
entries.authoritativeValue: Martell & Smith stepwise Cu2+/NH3 log K1..K4 = 4.04, 3.43, 2.80, 1.48 => log beta4 = 11.75 (25 C, zero ionic strength). Textbook formation constants: 1.7e13 (log 13.23, OpenStax/LibreTexts Lumen), 2.1e13 (13.32), 1.1e13 (13.04) - media/conditions unstated.
entries.source: Harvey, LibreTexts Formation Constants (cites Martell & Smith, Critical Stability Constants): https://chem.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Analytical_Chemistry/Analytical_Chemistry_Volume_I_(Harvey)/10%3A_Appendix/10.12%3A_Formation_Constants ; OpenStax Kf 1.7e13: https://chem.libretexts.org/Courses/Lumen_Learning/Book%3A_General_Chemistry__Lecture_and_Lab_(Lumen)/10%3A_Appendices/10.11%3A_Formation_Constants_for_Complex_Ions . NIST SRD 46 itself is distributed as Windows software and its tables could not be read online.
entries.note: PRIORITY. 13.0 agrees with common general-chemistry Kf (1.1e13) but is ~1.25 log units above the critical-compilation value at I = 0 (11.75), and I could not retrieve SRD 46 to see the I = 0.1 value. Higher-ionic-strength literature values (e.g. Bjerrum-type, I = 2 NH4NO3) were searched but not confirmed. Suggest relabelling 'log beta4 ~ 11.8 (I=0, Martell & Smith)' or 'about 12-13 depending on medium', and stating conditions on the figure. Source line to edit: src/lib/teaching/visual/conceptSceneParams.ts:783.

entries.figure: chem.coord.stability (conceptSceneParams.ts:779-786), Claim H
entries.authoritativeValue: 18.80, T = 20 C, mu = 0.1 M (Martell & Smith via Harvey). Metrohm monograph says its table is 25 C, I = 0.1 unless marked and flags Cu as 20 C. Same-table Cu2+/en: log K1 = 10.48, log K2 = 9.07 (25 C, I=0) => log beta2 = 19.55
entries.source: Harvey LibreTexts Formation Constants (URL in previous row); search-snippet corroboration from a Kawabe lanthanide-EDTA paper (not opened)
entries.note: Value matches; condition is 20 C / 0.1 M, not 25 C. FAIRNESS CAVEAT for the 'monodentate vs chelate' framing: the two bars differ in more than denticity - NH3 is a neutral 4-N donor set, EDTA (Y4-) is hexadentate N2O4 and 4- charged, and its log K refers to the fully deprotonated ligand (pH-dependent conditional constant is much lower, not looked up). The clean like-for-like chelate-effect comparison is 4 NH3 vs 2 en (same 4 N donors): 11.75 vs 19.55 at 25 C, I = 0 (both from the Harvey table, ~7.8 log units). Suggest adding a caveat or using Cu-en as the chelate bar. Mixed-ionic-strength note: NH3 constants are I=0, EDTA is I=0.1.

entries.source: Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrogen_selenide ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrogen_chalcogenide . NIST WebBook lists only an Antoine fit (Stull 1947); solving it at 1.01325 bar gives ~231.5 K (my calculation, not a stated value).
entries.note: No NIST-stated Tboil exists on the WebBook page; value rests on Greenwood & Earnshaw / CRC-type secondary quotes.

entries.figure: Claim I: Group 16 hydride normal boiling points
entries.authoritativeValue: 270.9 K (-2.2 C, Wikipedia infobox; decomposes above ~ -2 C); 269.15 K (-4 C, Greenwood & Earnshaw); NIST Stull Antoine solved at 1 atm ~271.5 K (my calculation)
entries.source: Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrogen_telluride ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrogen_chalcogenide ; https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/cbook.cgi?ID=C7783097&Mask=4
entries.note: Sources scatter by ~2 K and the compound is thermally unstable, so '~271 K' is an approximate value. The monotonic H2S<H2Se<H2Te trend and the H2O anomaly are correct.

entries.figure: Claim K: textbook facts
entries.authoritativeValue: 16 electrons, slightly distorted square planar by X-ray, d8 Rh(I)
entries.source: Wikipedia 'Wilkinson's catalyst': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilkinson%27s_catalyst

entries.figure: Claim K: textbook facts
entries.valueInFigure: PPh3 dissociation -> H2 oxidative addition -> alkene coordination -> migratory insertion -> reductive elimination
entries.authoritativeValue: Page lists exactly this order
entries.source: Wikipedia 'Wilkinson's catalyst' (URL above)
entries.note: This is the commonly presented order; the literature also discusses alkene-first/dihydride pathways (Halpern) - not checked here. Fine as a simplified teaching cycle.

entries.figure: Claim K: textbook facts
entries.quantity: Woodward-Hoffmann: [4+2] thermal ss allowed; [2+2] thermal forbidden, photochemical allowed
entries.authoritativeValue: Diels-Alder [pi4s+pi2s] allowed; [2+2] observed only photochemically for ordinary alkenes
entries.source: Wikipedia 'Woodward-Hoffmann rules': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodward%E2%80%93Hoffmann_rules

entries.figure: Claim K: textbook facts
entries.authoritativeValue: 4n e- conrotatory (thermal); 4n+2 disrotatory (thermal)
entries.source: Wikipedia 'Woodward-Hoffmann rules' (URL above)
entries.note: Reverses (disrotatory for 4n, conrotatory for 4n+2) under photochemical conditions.

entries.figure: Claim K: textbook facts

entries.authoritativeValue: [1,5]-H shifts facile; [1,3]-H shifts not observed thermally (would need antarafacial)
entries.source: Wikipedia 'Woodward-Hoffmann rules' (URL above)

entries.figure: Claim K: textbook facts
